worldmap.art-shop:
Art Supply Shop
Open 10:00AM to 6:00PM most days
shop.owner.canvas: Canvases are by the window. Don't buy the big ones until you've ruined a few small ones.
shop.owner.pigment: The pigments are ground fresh. Mostly. Don't sniff the cerulean.
shop.owner.brush: A good brush forgives you. A cheap one remembers everything.
shop.owner.selling: Selling? Let me see it. I'll give you a fair price. I'm the only one around here who knows what fair is.
shop.closed: Nobody's at the counter. Open 10am to 6pm (Fridays till 5, Sundays from 1). Closed Wednesdays.
sable.name: Sable
gift.love: Oh. Where did you find this? I'm keeping it somewhere the light can't fade it.$h
gift.dislike: ...I'll find a use for it. Probably.$u
gift.hate: No. Absolutely not. Take it back before it touches anything.$a
gift.neutral: Thanks. I'll put it on the shelf with the other mysteries.$0
dialogue.rainy: Rain's the best light there is. Flat and honest. Nothing to hide behind.#$b#...I'm painting inside today anyway. The canvases hate the damp.
intro.02: Oh. A customer. Or a lost farmer. Same thing, in my experience.$u#$b#I'm Sable. This is the shop. Canvases, pigments, brushes. And I buy paintings, if you make any worth buying.
intro.03: Here. Three canvases, a palette and a jar of rose. The first ones are free. That's how they get you.$h
intro.04: The board's for commissions. People in town want paintings of the things they love. Paint them well and they'll pay you. They'll like you more, too.#$b#The counter's open ten till six. Go make something.
dialogue.AcceptBouquet: Is that... for me?$6#$b#I don't have anything clever to say. That's never happened before.$l
dialogue.RejectBouquet_VeryLowHearts: Flowers. For me. We've spoken, what, twice? Put them in water before they die of embarrassment.$u
dialogue.RejectBouquet_LowHearts: That's... sweet. Ask me again when I know what color your eyes are in the evening.$l
dialogue.RejectBouquet: Not yet. But don't throw those away.$l
dialogue.RejectMermaidPendant: That's a very serious shade of blue. Give me time to get used to it.$l
dialogue.RejectMermaidPendant_NeedHouseU: Where would I put my easel? Your house is one room and a bad smell. Talk to Robin first.$u
dialogue.dating_Sable: So we're... a thing. I need to sit down. I'm going to sit down.$l
engagement.0: ...Yes. Obviously yes.$l#$b#Give me a second, I'm mixing a lot of feelings at once.$h
engagement.1: Lewis says we'll be married in a few days. I've started three paintings of you and finished none of them. That's normal. That's fine.$l
mail.grand-opening: Hello, new neighbor.^I've opened an art supply shop in Cindersap Forest, west of the path down from Marnie's. Canvases, pigments, brushes and frames, and I buy paintings, if you ever pick up a brush.^I've put two canvases in with this. No pressure. (Some pressure.)^Open 10am to 6pm (Fridays till 5, Sundays from 1). Closed Wednesdays.^   -Sable
mail.grand-opening.title: The art shop opens
dialogue.WinterStar_GiveGift_Before: Happy Winter Star. I'm your secret friend. I made you something, so be nice about it.
dialogue.WinterStar_GiveGift_After: I've watched you carry those past the shop all year. I thought you should have one that keeps.$h
dialogue.WinterStar_GiveGift_Before_Spou: Happy Winter Star, love. Of course I drew your name. I may have arranged it.
dialogue.WinterStar_GiveGift_After_Spous: You carry those past me every day. Now there's one that keeps. I love you.$l
dialogue.Introduction: ...Hello. You must be the new farmer.$6#$b#You've brought half your field in on your boots. Good soil, though. I can tell.$u#$e#I'm Sable. I run the art shop in the forest. I sell paint, and I buy paintings. If you ever make one, I'll tell you the truth about it.
dialogue.Mon: $c 0.50#Mondays are for priming canvases. Nothing exciting happens on a Monday. That's the point.#Gesso, sand, gesso, sand. Mondays are very glamorous.$u
dialogue.Mon2: You keep coming back. Either you like the shop or you're lost.$u#$e#The forest's that way. The shop's right here.
dialogue.Mon4: $c 0.50#I did a study of the river this morning. Just the reflections. The water itself is boring. The light on it isn't.#Morning light comes in low over the river. Everything gets a gold edge for about twenty minutes. Then it's gone.
dialogue.Mon6: $c 0.50#I left a small canvas out for you at the shop, by the window. Don't make it a big deal.$l#I sharpened every pencil I own this morning and then didn't draw a thing. I was thinking. About things.$u
dialogue.Mon8: I caught myself mixing your farm's colors this morning. Field green. Barn red. Fresh-turned soil.$l#$b#...I don't know why I'm telling you this.$u
dialogue.Mon10: Monday again. I used to dread them. Now I just think, good, a whole week of you wandering in.$l
dialogue.Tue: $c 0.50#Pigment comes from everything. Stones, roots, beetles. Mostly stones. Don't ask about the beetles.#Clay from the riverbank makes a lovely red earth. It makes a lovely mess, too.$u
dialogue.Tue2: $c 0.50#If you're grinding your own pigment, use a glass muller. Not your coffee mug. I know from experience.$u#You can tell a cheap brush by the way it sheds. You can tell a cheap painter by the way they blame the brush.
dialogue.Tue4: $c 0.50#The stones from the mines grind into the best colors. Amethyst for violet, ruby for red. Aquamarine, if you're feeling rich.#Bring me something shiny from the mines and I'll show you what color it really is underneath.
dialogue.Tue6: $c 0.50#Most people paint what they think they see. You paint what's there. That's rarer than talent.#You hold a brush like a hoe. ...That wasn't an insult. You hold it like it has work to do.$u
dialogue.Tue8: I mixed a new green yesterday. I'm calling it 'your farm at seven in the morning'. It won't fit on the label.$l
dialogue.Wed: $c 0.50#The shop's closed on Wednesdays. I'm not. Talk away.#Wednesday. No customers, no counter. Just me and whatever I'm avoiding painting.
dialogue.Wed2: $c 0.50#I spend Wednesdays looking at other people's old work. It's either research or procrastination. Probably both.$u#Wednesdays I don't touch a brush until noon. Rest your eyes and they come back sharper.
dialogue.Wed4: $c 0.50#Gunther lets me look at the old pieces before they go behind glass. Don't tell anyone. He'll get requests.$u#The dwarf scrolls at the museum have wonderful linework. Whoever drew them never once lifted the pen.
dialogue.Wed6: Evelyn makes the worst tea in the valley. I go every week.$h#$e#She has a good eye, you know. She notices where light lands. That isn't common.
dialogue.Wed8: Evelyn asked about you. I said you were 'fine'. She gave me a look. Apparently I said it wrong.$l
dialogue.Thu: $c 0.50#Sand the frame before you stain it. Every step you skip shows up later.#A good frame should disappear. If people notice the frame, the frame's wrong.
dialogue.Thu2: $c 0.50#Varnish goes on last. Always last. Patience is most of this job.#Someone tried to return a canvas because it was 'too white'. I sold them a smaller one.$u
dialogue.Thu4: $c 0.50#A painting is mostly decisions about what to leave out. People think it's about putting things in.#Squint at what you're painting. The details go, and the shapes are what's left. Paint the shapes.
dialogue.Thu6: I used to restore paintings for a living. Other people's. You learn exactly where every brushstroke went.#$b#You also learn exactly where they gave up.$s
dialogue.Thu8: I used to think I fixed paintings so I'd never have to finish one of my own.$s#$b#You're ruining that for me.$l
dialogue.Fri: $c 0.50#Fridays I close early and go to the Saloon. Leah tells me sculpture is color. I tell her it's furniture.$u#Friday. Gus does a cheese plate I would paint if I didn't eat it first.
dialogue.Fri2: Emily came in for fabric dye again. I don't sell fabric dye. She bought pigment anyway. I respect that.$h
dialogue.Fri4: $c 0.50#Elliott asked me to paint the cover for his book. I said yes before he finished the sentence. Don't tell him.$h#Leah carved a heron out of driftwood. I've been jealous all week. Wood doesn't need mixing.$u
dialogue.Fri6: $c 0.50#You should come to the Saloon tonight. Not for me. The lamplight in there is very forgiving.$u#If you're at the Saloon tonight, sit where the lamp is behind you. Trust me. Everyone looks better.
dialogue.Fri8: Sit with me at the Saloon tonight. Elliott's reading again. I'll need someone to make faces at.$u
dialogue.Sat: $c 0.50#Saturdays, people come in to buy one brush and leave with six. I don't make the rules.#Saturday crowd. Two browsers, one buyer, and Jas asking if paint is edible. It isn't.
dialogue.Sat2: $c 0.50#Robin builds my stretcher bars. Perfectly square, every time. I could cry.$h#Pierre asked if paintings sell better with a farm in them. I told him everything sells better with a farm in it.$u
dialogue.Sat4: $c 0.50#Bring me your next painting before you sell it. Not for a price. I just want to see it.#If a painting isn't working, turn it upside down. You'll see what's wrong with it in a second.
dialogue.Sat6: $c 0.50#Clint bought one of the commission paintings. He held it like it might break. It might.#Abigail bought violet again. That's three jars this season. Whatever she's painting, it's very purple.
dialogue.Sat8: There's an easel in the back with a canvas I keep turning to face the wall.$s#$e#Maybe one day I'll turn it around.
dialogue.Sun: $c 0.50#Sundays I paint the sea. It never holds still. Good lesson in letting go.#The tide doesn't care what I'm painting. I've lost two easels to it.$u
dialogue.Sun2: Willy watched me paint the boats for an hour. Then he said, 'that's the wrong boat'. It was.$u
dialogue.Sun4: $c 0.50#Salt air is hard on canvas. I don't care. The light by the sea is worth it.#Elliott walks past while I paint and narrates. Out loud. Under his breath, he thinks.$u
dialogue.Sun6: $c 0.50#The sea was gray this morning. Eleven grays. I counted.$h#I painted the beach this morning and left a little figure in the corner. It looks a bit like you. Coincidence.$l
dialogue.Sun8: I've started signing my paintings again. Just an S. I got the idea from someone.$l
dialogue.spring_Mon: $c 0.50#Spring is all yellow-green. Nobody believes me until they try to mix it.#New leaves are the hardest green. Too much yellow and they're sickly. Too little and they're summer.
dialogue.spring_Tue: Rain, sun, rain, sun. Spring can't decide on a palette either.
dialogue.spring_Wed: Everything's in bloom out there. It's almost vulgar.$u
dialogue.spring_Thu: Cherry blossom is the hardest pink. Too much white and it's chalk. Too little and it's ham.$u
dialogue.spring_Fri: Sweet peas are out. That's the color I'd keep if I could only keep one.
dialogue.spring_Sat: $c 0.50#Everyone wants to paint flowers in spring. I let them. Then I sell them more green.#Spring stock: more green, more yellow, more patience.
dialogue.spring_Sun: The beach in spring is mostly wind. Hard to paint wind. You paint what it does to everything else.
dialogue.summer_Mon: In summer I paint at the river. The light's too sharp by noon, so it's an early start.
dialogue.summer_Tue: Oils dry slower in this humidity. Watercolors dry faster. Everything's working against everybody.$u
dialogue.summer_Wed: The museum's cool in summer. That's not why I go. ...It's partly why I go.$u
dialogue.summer_Thu: Bring me a fairy rose and I'll give you a discount. Don't hold me to that.
dialogue.summer_Fri: Fireflies are pure light on dark. You can't paint them. I keep trying.
dialogue.summer_Sat: $c 0.50#The shop gets hot by afternoon. The paint gets lazy. So do I.#Summer Saturdays I sell more sun hats' worth of yellow than anything else. Everyone paints the sun.
dialogue.summer_Sun: Right before nine, the water goes the color of a fresh bruise. I wait for it every week.
dialogue.fall_Mon: Fall is the season that does the painting for you. It's almost unfair.$h
dialogue.fall_Tue: Ochre, sienna, umber. All the earth colors come out to play.
dialogue.fall_Wed: The museum gets fall light through the high windows. Everything in there looks a hundred years older. Which it is.
dialogue.fall_Thu: $c 0.50#People think fall is orange. Look closer. It's about forty colors pretending to be orange.#Fall shadows are purple. Once you see it you can't stop.
dialogue.fall_Fri: Fall evenings at the Saloon. Everyone in sweaters. Very good palette, the Saloon in fall.
dialogue.fall_Sat: Leaves press nicely between canvases. I ruined three canvases learning that.$u
dialogue.fall_Sun: The beach is empty in fall. That's my favorite kind of beach.
dialogue.winter_Mon: Too cold to paint outside. Paint goes thick and sulky in the cold. Me too.$s
dialogue.winter_Tue: $c 0.50#Snow isn't white. It's blue in the shadows and pink in the sun. Never white.#Winter light is thin. It makes everything look like a drawing. I like that.
dialogue.winter_Wed: Evelyn knits while I sketch. Then she critiques my sketch, and I critique her knitting. It's lovely.$h
dialogue.winter_Thu: Winter's for framing. Measure twice, cut once, swear quietly.
dialogue.winter_Fri: Night comes so early in winter. I lock up in the dark and the windows glow. I like that part.
dialogue.winter_Sat: If you want to give someone a painting for the Winter Star, start it now. Not the night before. I'm looking at you.$u
dialogue.winter_Sun: The sea's wilder in winter. I paint it from further back.
dialogue.Beach: Don't stand in my light. ...No, you're fine. You're in a good spot, actually.$u
dialogue.ArchaeologyHouse: Look at the glaze on that pot. Someone took their time, a thousand years ago.
dialogue.JoshHouse: Evelyn's showing me her garden notes. She sketches every flower she plants. Did you know that?
dialogue.Saloon: Leah says sculpture counts as color. Elliott's on her side. Sit down, you can be the tiebreaker.$u
dialogue.fall_9: You remembered. Or the calendar did. Either way.$l
dialogue.spring_1: A new year. New canvases. Same hands.
dialogue.summer_1: Summer. Everything will be too bright for a while.
dialogue.winter_1: Winter. The shop's warm, if you want somewhere to stand.
dialogue.FlowerDance_Accept: Dance? With me?$6#$b#...Alright. I'll lead. You'll step on my feet anyway.$l
dialogue.FlowerDance_Decline: I don't dance. I sketch the people who do.$u
dialogue.Resort_Entering: I've never seen water that color. I'm going to spend the whole day failing to paint it.$h
dialogue.Resort_Leaving: Back to the valley. My eyes need a rest from all this turquoise.
dialogue.Resort: Everything here is too bright to paint. I'm trying anyway.$u
dialogue.Resort_Shore: The color of the shallows changes every few feet. I've counted nine blues. There are more.
dialogue.Resort_Wander: Look at the green on these leaves. Back home it'd look fake.$h
dialogue.Resort_Bar: Something with a tiny umbrella. For research.$u
dialogue.Resort_Chair: I'm not lying down. I'm studying the light from a lower angle.$u
dialogue.AcceptGift_66: Amethyst. I can get three jars of violet out of this. Thank you.$h
dialogue.AcceptGift_64: A ruby. You know what the old painters paid for red like this? Everything.$h
dialogue.AcceptGift_595: A fairy rose. It's the exact color I can never mix. Thank you.$l
dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Positive: For my birthday? ...Thank you. I'll keep it somewhere I can see it.$l
dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Negative: For my birthday. Well. It's the thought.$u
marriage.Rainy_Day_0: Rain on the roof, coffee on the stove, nowhere to be. I'm going to paint until the light gives up.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_1: I left you some coffee. It's the good beans. Don't tell the shop's accountant. (It's me.)[(O)395]$u
marriage.Rainy_Day_2: Flat gray light. Every color tells the truth on days like this.
marriage.Rainy_Day_3: The canvases warp in the damp. I've moved them all into the kitchen. Sorry.$u
marriage.Rainy_Day_4: Don't track mud on my drop cloth. ...Actually, do. It's a good umber.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_0: You're soaked. Sit by the stove. I'll make tea, badly, like Evelyn taught me.
marriage.Rainy_Night_1: I painted the rain on the window all afternoon. It's terrible. I'm keeping it.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_2: Listen to it. Like someone washing brushes on the roof.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_3: I found mud on the ceiling. I've decided not to ask.$u
marriage.Rainy_Night_4: Come here. You're the warmest thing in this house.$l
marriage.Indoor_Day_0: Good morning. There's paint on the kettle. I don't know how either.$u
marriage.Indoor_Day_1: I made you something small. Don't make a fuss.[(O)blinxxy.MuseArt_Canvas_Small (O)blinxxy.MuseArt_Pigment_rose]$l
marriage.Indoor_Day_2: The light in this house is all wrong in the morning and perfect at four. I've planned my life around four.
marriage.Indoor_Day_3: I sketched you while you were asleep. You snore in ochre.$u
marriage.Indoor_Day_4: Coffee's on. I may have used the brush water by mistake. Taste it first.$u
marriage.Indoor_Night_0: Sit still. No, like that. ...Okay, you can move. I've got your hands.
marriage.Indoor_Night_1: Ten years I didn't paint. Now I can't stop. I'm blaming you.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_2: Evelyn says hello. She also says you need to eat more vegetables, which is rich, coming from her.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_3: I keep looking at the pendant. I've mixed a hundred blues. None of them were this one.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_4: Don't look in the studio corner yet. It's not finished. It's never finished. Go to sleep.$u
marriage.Outdoor_0: The light on the crops this morning... hold on, I need a pencil.$h
marriage.Outdoor_1: Your fields are a patchwork. Every square a different green. You've made a painting and you don't even know it.
marriage.Outdoor_2: Wind's from the west. The clouds will be good by noon.
marriage.Outdoor_3: Don't work yourself into the ground. I'm not painting you as a scarecrow.$u
marriage.Outdoor_4: Some of the best colors I own came from this farm.$h
marriage.Good_1: I used to think a finished painting was a failure waiting to be noticed. Now I think it's just a finished painting.$h
marriage.Good_2: You look good in this light. You look good in most light. I've checked.$l
marriage.Good_3: Hold still. You've got a smudge. ...There. Now it's a better smudge.$u
marriage.Good_4: When you came into the shop that first time, I thought you were lost. You were. So was I.$l
marriage.Good_5: I sold a painting today. One of mine. A woman from Zuzu City cried a little.#$b#I may have cried a little too.$h
marriage.Good_6: Be careful in the mines. I need you in one piece. I've only painted you in one piece.
marriage.Good_7: Thank you for ruining my quiet, empty life.$l
marriage.Neutral_0: Morning. I'm thinking about the color of toast. Don't interrupt.
marriage.Neutral_1: The shop's slow this week. Everyone's busy planting. Including you.
marriage.Neutral_2: If you're going into town, Pierre owes me for six frames.
marriage.Neutral_3: I need more umber. I always need more umber.
marriage.Neutral_4: The kitchen table is a still life now. Please don't eat it.$u
marriage.Neutral_5: Do you think a cow would sit for a portrait? Asking for no reason.
marriage.Bad_0: You haven't looked at anything I've painted in weeks.$s
marriage.Bad_1: I'm painting things that are empty again. I know what that means.$s
marriage.Bad_2: The critic was half right, you know. I'm technically flawless. Lately I'm also completely alone.$s
marriage.Bad_3: ...Do you still like being here? With me?$s
marriage.Bad_4: I've started fixing other people's paintings again. It's easier than talking to you.$s
marriage.patio_Sable: Don't look yet. It's your barn at sunrise. The barn is cooperating. The sunrise isn't.$u
marriage.spouseRoom_Sable: This corner gets the north light. Every painter wants the north light. I got it by marrying a farmer.$l
marriage.funLeave_Sable: I'm going to paint by the river today. I'll be back before the light goes.
marriage.funReturn_Sable: I painted the river and the river won. How was your day?$h
marriage.jobLeave_Sable: I'm off to open the shop. Don't let the chickens near my easel.
marriage.jobReturn_Sable: Sold four canvases and a very expensive brush. I'm a magnate now. What's for dinner?$h
marriage.OneKid_0: %kid1 painted the dog. And the floor. And the dog again. I'm so proud.$h
marriage.TwoKids_0: Two little painters. The walls never stood a chance.$h
marriage.spring_1: A new year. I've bought far too many canvases for it.$h
marriage.summer_1: Summer. Everything's too bright to paint and I'm going to try anyway.$u
marriage.fall_1: Fall. My season. Try to keep up.$h
marriage.fall_9: You remembered my birthday. You always do. ...I've painted you something. It's in the studio corner.$l
marriage.winter_1: Snow on the farm. Blue in the shadows, pink in the sun. Come and look.$l
festival.spring13: Every egg in this town is painted by hand. Badly. I love it.$h#$e#Look at that one. Purple with yellow dots. Somebody meant that.
festival.spring24: Everything's one pink today. The petals, the dresses, the punch.$u#$e#...It's lovely. Don't tell anyone I said so.
festival.summer11: Lewis asked if I'd paint the governor's portrait for the town hall. I said I'd think about it.$u#$e#I've thought about it.
festival.summer28: I've tried for years to mix that glow. Nothing on any palette comes close.$s#$e#Maybe that's the point. Some things you just look at.
festival.fall16: I'm painting signs for anyone who wants one. Three customers so far, and one of them was a dog.$h#$e#He wanted his name in red. Good taste.
festival.fall27: The maze is a composition problem, if you think about it. Mostly negative space.$u#$e#...I got lost twice.
festival.winter8: Ice sculpture. All the work of marble, and it's gone by spring.$s#$e#I respect that more than I can say.
festival.winter25: Happy Winter Star. Everything's red and gold and candlelit. It's like standing inside an old master.$h
mail.collection50: Fifty different subjects. I counted, because of course I did.^Most painters find three things they're good at and paint those until they die. You keep looking at new things. That's the whole job, really.^This brush was my teacher's. It's wasted in a drawer.^   -Sable
mail.collection50.title: Fifty subjects
mail.portfolio-seasons: Four seasons of the same street. You'd be amazed how few painters have the patience.^The town looks different every time because you do. Here's a cabinet for curing your work. Don't rush it.^   -Sable
mail.portfolio-seasons.title: The Four Seasons
mail.portfolio-harvest: A page of things you grew and then painted. Twice the work, and twice the right to be proud of it.^Here's a mill. Grind your own colours. It's cheaper than buying them from me, which I shouldn't be telling you.^   -Sable
mail.portfolio-harvest.title: Harvest
mail.portfolio-fine-work: Gold, iridium, glazed, varnished, and a Masterpiece. I looked at that page for a long time.^Linen, for the next one.^   -Sable
mail.portfolio-fine-work.title: Fine Work
mail.portfolio-far-places: Desert sand, island light, the dark of the cavern. You went a long way for that page.^Linen, the big kind. Paint somewhere far away on it.^   -Sable
mail.portfolio-far-places.title: Far Places
mail.portfolio-legends: Five fish nobody believes in, and you painted every one of them from life.^This palette holds more than you'll need. Good. Fill it anyway.^   -Sable
mail.portfolio-legends.title: Legends
mail.collection-wreck: The Wreck's paintings hang together now, the whole voyage. A fisherman stood in front of the storm for an hour yesterday.^I had these frames made from driftwood off the beach, for your own seascapes.^   -Gunther
mail.collection-wreck.title: The Wreck, complete
mail.collection-miners: Every one of the Miners' paintings is on the wall. Clint came in and didn't say anything, which from Clint is high praise.^Iron frames, riveted the old way. For your own work.^   -Gunther
mail.collection-miners.title: The Miners, complete
mail.collection-calico: Calico's paintings, all four, together for the first time in who knows how long. Sandy cried. I may have as well.^Sandstone frames, carved in the old desert style.^   -Gunther
mail.collection-calico.title: Calico, complete
mail.collection-dwarvish: Both Dwarvish paintings, side by side. The dwarf in the mines came up to see them, and bowed to the king.^A Dwarvish frame, or two. Bronze, with a stone in it. Don't ask how I came by them.^   -Gunther
mail.collection-dwarvish.title: The Dwarves, complete
order.lewis.name: Faces for the Town Hall
order.lewis.text: The town hall's walls are bare, and Lewis thinks portraits of the townsfolk would make it feel more like everyone's. He'd like three, by a local painter.
order.lewis.objective: Bring Lewis three portraits of villagers
order.lewis.thanks: Look at that. It's like having half the town over for tea. Thank you, @.
mail.order-lewis: The portraits are up in the town hall, and folks keep stopping to find themselves. Marnie says hers is "very flattering, almost suspicious".^Here are a few frames, so you can hang some of your own at home.^   -Lewis
mail.order-lewis.title: Faces for the Town Hall
order.gus.name: Art for the Saloon
order.gus.text: Gus wants something on the Saloon's walls besides the dartboard: paintings of good food and drink, to make his customers hungry and thirsty.
order.gus.objective: Bring Gus two gold-quality paintings of food or drink
order.gus.thanks: Now that's a meal you can't eat, and I can't stop looking at it! Up on the wall they go.
mail.order-gus: Pam says she gets thirsty just looking at the wall now. Business is up.^A friend of mine trades in pigments. He says this red is the colour of a good wine.^   -Gus
mail.order-gus.title: Art for the Saloon
order.leah.name: The Secret Woods
order.leah.text: Leah's been trying to sketch the Secret Woods all year, and she says the light keeps beating her. She'd love to see how another painter sees it.
order.leah.objective: Bring Leah a view painted in the Secret Woods
order.leah.thanks: Oh. You got the light. I've been trying to get that light for months! Can I keep it? I'm keeping it.
mail.order-leah: I hung your painting by my bed. I look at it every morning, and then I go and try again.^This brush was my first good one. It's too fine for how I paint now. I think it's more yours.^   -Leah
mail.order-leah.title: The Secret Woods
order.elliott.name: The Beach by Moonlight
order.elliott.text: Elliott wants a painting of the beach at night for his cabin, "to look at when the words won't come." It has to be painted there, after dark.
order.elliott.objective: Bring Elliott a view of the beach, painted at night
order.elliott.thanks: The sea, at night, by the light of a lamp. You've painted the very thing I keep failing to write.
mail.order-elliott: Your painting hangs over my writing desk now. I have written four chapters since. Coincidence, I'm sure.^Sable tells me these are the frames for night paintings.^   -Elliott
mail.order-elliott.title: The Beach by Moonlight
order.qi.name: A Legend in Oils
order.qi.text: Any fool can catch a legend, given time. Paint one so well it would hang in a museum, and ship it to me.
order.qi.objective: Ship a Masterpiece of a legendary fish
mail.portfolio-faces: A whole page of faces. Everyone looks a little startled, which is how you know they're good likenesses.^Frames, for the ones you hang. Faces like a little moonlight.^   -Sable
mail.portfolio-faces.title: Faces of the Valley
mail.portfolio-book: Every page. Every single one. I sat with the book for an hour before I could write this.^I had this frame made for you. Gold leaf, the real kind. Put your favourite in it.^There's one page left, and it isn't in the book yet. Paint the view from the top of the valley.^   -Sable
mail.portfolio-book.title: The Portfolio
wedding.vows: @... %spouse...#$b#As the mayor of Pelican Town, and regional bearer of the matrimonial seal, I now pronounce you... married!$h
yard.painting.0: The river bend, before the light flattens it.#$b#Don't stand in my sun.
yard.painting.1: Marnie's fence. It's crooked in a way I can't stop looking at.
yard.painting.2: Just the grass.$u#$b#Green is the hardest colour there is. Everyone thinks they know it.
yard.painting.3: The shop, from out here.#$b#Strange, painting your own front door.
yard.painting.4: The path down from Marnie's, with nobody on it yet. That never lasts.
yard.painting.5: Clouds. They won't hold still, which is rude of them.$h
event.sable2h.01: Oh. It's after hours.$6#$b#...You can stay. Don't touch anything.
event.sable2h.02: It's a landscape. Cindersap Forest, about forty years ago. The museum sent it to me to restore. I was meant to send it back.
event.sable2h.03: Look at the light on the water. Whoever painted this stood right where my shop is now. Same river, same bend.$s
event.sable2h.04: It's signed 'E.' Just the initial. No records. Nobody knows who painted it.
event.sable2h.05: I kept it. Then I quit my job and moved here. It's why I'm here.#$b#Don't laugh.$u
event.sable2h.08: Who do you think E. was?
event.sable2h.09: ...Brave is a strong word. Stubborn, maybe.$l
event.sable2h.11: Somebody who loved this valley. You can see it in how they did the water.$h
event.sable2h.12: Go home, farmer. The light's gone.
event.sable6h.01: The Zuzu City Museum wants me back. Head of restoration. Double the pay, my old studio. A window.$s
event.sable6h.02: I told myself I came here for the painting. But I've been restoring it for a year. I could finish it tomorrow.
event.sable6h.03: I haven't painted anything of my own in ten years.#$b#A critic called my work 'technically flawless and completely empty'. I believed them.#$b#It was easier to fix other people's work. You can't fail at someone else's painting.$s
event.sable6h.05: It's your call. I'll miss you either way.
event.sable6h.07: ...You'd say that to anyone who sells you canvases.#$b#No. You wouldn't.$l
event.sable6h.08: That's the worst possible answer. It's also the kind one.$s
event.sable6h.09: Something of mine?$6#$b#...Fine. One thing. Then I'll decide.
event.sable10h.01: It's the first original I've finished in ten years.#$b#Don't say anything until you've looked at it properly.
event.sable10h.02: Sable pulls the sheet away. It's a portrait of you.
event.sable10h.03: Technically flawless. Completely full.$l#$b#...That's what the critic should have said about this one.
event.sable10h.04: It's the best thing I've ever seen.
event.sable10h.06: You haven't seen many paintings.#$b#...I'll take it.$l
event.sable10h.08: It's yours. Hang it somewhere I can see it when I visit.$l
event.sable14h.01: Sable's paintings fill the walls and the panels across the floor, Evelyn's landscape and your portrait among them. In the middle stands a Junimo made of paint tubes.
event.sable14h.02: A real gallery, in our little valley! This is going in the newsletter.
event.sable14h.03: This one has... sculptural color. Don't tell Sable I said that.$h
event.sable14h.04: And so the evening unfolded, every canvas a window into a quieter heart...
event.sable14h.05: Okay, fine. Painting is kind of cool. Does Sable teach lessons?
event.sable14h.06: I built every one of those frames, you know. Just saying.
event.sable14h.07: Forty years, and it's back on a wall in the forest. Isn't that something, George?
event.sable14h.08: Hmph. Best painting in the room.#$b#...After the farmer's.
event.sable14h.09: Ten years of nothing. Then one farmer walks in with half a field on their boots.$l
event.sable14h.10: Thank you for ruining my quiet, empty life.$h
event.sable4h.01: You're late. I set up a canvas for you an hour ago.$u
event.sable4h.02: Let me see.#$b#Your water is all one blue. Water's never one blue.
event.sable4h.03: When you mix, don't chase the color. Let it come to you. Hold steady, and only move when it moves.
event.sable4h.04: Here. It's the first good brush I ever owned. It's been in a drawer for ten years.#$b#It should be painting.$l
event.sable4h.05: Sable's canvas is a careful pencil sketch. There's no paint on it.
event.sable4h.07: You never finish them, do you?
event.sable4h.10: It's a sketch. But... thank you.$l
event.sable8h.01: I wanted you to see this, Evelyn. You know the forest better than anyone.
event.sable8h.02: Sable unwraps a small landscape from brown paper: the river bend in Cindersap Forest, signed 'E.'
event.sable8h.04: I painted this. The summer before I married George. I sat on the riverbank every morning for a month.
event.sable8h.06: Evelyn. I always signed with just the E. I thought it looked very mysterious.$h#$b#I gave it to a traveling dealer for a song. We needed the money for the farm.
event.sable8h.07: I stopped painting after that. There was always something more useful to do. You know how it is.
event.sable8h.08: She was good, too. Better than good.
event.sable8h.09: Oh, hush.#$b#...Sable, dear. Would you paint with me one morning? I'm slow now. My hands shake.
event.sable8h.10: I'd like that more than anything.$l
event.sable8h.11: Sable and Evelyn talk about the river bend and old brushes until the tea goes cold.
letter.stay: I tore the letter up this morning.$l#$b#Don't look so pleased with yourself.$u
letter.your-call: I made my call. The letter's in the stove.$s#$b#...I'm staying. I'm not sure I'd have decided that if you'd made it for me.
letter.paint-first: I wrote back and said I needed a season to think.$u#$b#Then I bought myself a canvas. From my own shop. Retail price.$h
evelyn.Wed: Sable and I painted the river bend this morning. My hands remembered more than I thought they would.$h
evelyn.Sat: I found my old brushes in the attic. George says they smell like the summer before we married.$h
julian.name: Julian
julian.gift.love: This is genuinely good. I'm as surprised as you are.$6
julian.gift.hate: Is this a review? It reads like one.$a
julian.dialogue.Introduction: Julian Vane, The Zuzu Review. No, you won't have read it.#$b#You must be the farmer who paints. Mud on your cuffs, cerulean on your thumb. Promising.$u
julian.dialogue.spring_22: Spring in the valley. Everything is green and earnest and trying very hard.#$b#I'll be in your portfolio, if anyone asks.$u
julian.dialogue.spring_23: The sea here is a very convincing blue. Someone should tell it nobody paints seascapes any more.$u
julian.dialogue.spring_24: Last day. I've looked through your portfolio twice. From me, that's a compliment.$0
julian.dialogue.summer_22: It's thirty degrees and I'm wearing wool. Don't. I'm aware.$a
julian.dialogue.summer_23: Your museum has a very good meteorite and a very bad lamp. I've written to someone about the lamp.$7
julian.dialogue.summer_24: Is everyone here always this pleasant? It's unnerving.$6
julian.dialogue.fall_22: Fall. Finally, a season with some taste.$u
julian.dialogue.fall_23: I judged your fair's painting contest last week. I'm still recovering from the pumpkin entries.$u
julian.dialogue.fall_24: The light in that forest this time of year...#$b#Don't quote me.$7
julian.dialogue.winter_22: It's my birthday, since you ask. You didn't. I'm telling you anyway.$u
julian.dialogue.winter_23: Snow is the only honest critic. It covers everything equally.$7
julian.dialogue.winter_24: Back to the city tomorrow. Grey and loud and full of people who agree with me. I can hardly wait.$s
sable.julian-visit.22: He's in town. Don't ask me who. I'll be at my easel.$a
sable.julian-visit.23: If a man in a long coat asks about me, I've emigrated.$u
julian.item.catalogue.description: The catalogue from a small gallery show in Zuzu City, ten years ago. There's a note in pencil in one margin. Julian asked you to give it to Sable.
contest.festival: The painting contest. Bring me something worth judging.$u
contest.tourist: I came all the way from Zuzu City to see the painting contest. That's Julian Vane judging! He once called a sculpture "a shrug in bronze." I hope he's kinder today.
sable.catalogue.cold: Where did you get this?$a#$b#...Put it in the stove.$a#$b#No. Give it here. I'll do it myself.
sable.catalogue.warm: This is from my first show. Where did you...$6#$b#There's writing. Next to the third one.#$b#'Not empty.'$6#$b#...Ten years. He wrote this ten years ago.$s#$b#Thank you for bringing it. I don't know what I'll do with it yet.$s
julian-event.julian2h.01: Don't hover. Come and look with me.$7
julian-event.julian2h.02: This page. The first one is careful. The second is clever. The third...$7
julian-event.julian2h.07: ...Did they.$s#$b#They were always a good teacher. Even when nobody asked.$s
julian-event.julian2h.08: Neither of them speaks. Sable takes a box of frames from beside the door and leaves.
julian-event.julian2h.09: Well. That was the warmest welcome I've had in years.$u
julian-event.julian4h.01: Your museum has room for exactly one painting. I've been deciding which of yours.$u
julian-event.julian4h.02: But that's what I think. What were you trying to do?$7
julian-event.julian4h.04: Make it feel like the place.
julian-event.julian4h.06: Then you did. Exactness is underrated. People only call it cold when they're afraid of it.$0
julian-event.julian4h.07: Then you did that too. That's the harder one.$h
julian-event.julian4h.08: ...That's the best answer anyone's given me in twenty years.$l
julian-event.julian4h.09: We don't actually have a painting wall.
julian-event.julian6h.01: The evening bus pulls away without him.
julian-event.julian6h.02: I missed it. On purpose.$u#$b#Don't tell anyone. It would ruin me.$u
julian-event.julian6h.03: Ten years ago I reviewed a young painter's first show. I wrote one sentence about it that everyone still quotes.$0#$b#'Technically flawless and completely empty.'$0
julian-event.julian6h.04: I wrote it because it sounded good. I was right about the first half.$s
julian-event.julian6h.05: He takes an old exhibition catalogue from inside his coat. In the margin, next to the third painting, in pencil: 'the third one is not empty.'
julian-event.julian6h.06: I wrote that the same night. I never published it. It didn't sound as good.$s
julian-event.julian6h.10: I know. I've known for ten years. Knowing is the easy part.$s
julian-event.julian6h.11: Because you're the only person here who looks at both of us like we're worth looking at.$7
julian-event.julian6h.12: A critic's dream. An audience that doesn't argue.$h
julian-event.julian6h.13: Lewis has offered to drive me back to the city tonight. I've told him what I think of his truck. He's driving me anyway.$u
julian-event.julian8h.01: Julian sits alone with a glass of wine he hasn't touched. The catalogue lies on the table in front of him.
julian-event.julian8h.02: I've tried to walk into that shop four times. I get as far as the yard.$s
julian-event.julian8h.03: Would you give them this? Not from me. Just... give it to them.$s
julian-event.julian8h.05: You should give it to them yourself.
julian-event.julian8h.06: Thank you.$l#$b#That's two people in this valley I've said that to. Don't let it get around.$u
julian-event.julian8h.07: I know what I should do. I'm asking what you'll do.$a#$b#...Please.$s
julian-event.julian10h.01: Sable stands at an easel with a painting of their own: the river bend, the light flat on the water. Julian is in the doorway.
julian-event.julian10h.02: You can say it. You've had ten years to work on it.$a
julian-event.julian10h.03: Julian takes out his notebook, and reads.
julian-event.julian10h.04: 'The river bend, at the hour the light lies flat on the water. Ten years ago I called this painter's work technically flawless and completely empty.'$7#$b#'I was wrong. This painting might not be technically flawless, but it is perfect in its own right.'$l
julian-event.julian10h.05: 'Perfect in its own right.' You'd never have written that ten years ago.$u#$b#...Thank you, Julian.$l
julian-event.julian10h.06: I'll be back next season. To review the next one.$h
julian-after.sable: Julian's in town. He's buying the coffee this time.$u
margot.name: Margot
margot.gift.love: Oh! Oh, you shouldn't have. You absolutely should have. Thank you!$h
margot.gift.like: That's lovely, thank you. I'll find it a good shelf.$h
margot.gift.dislike: Ah. Thank you. I'll... file that.$s
margot.gift.hate: Please don't bring that near the paintings. Or near me.$a
margot.dialogue.Introduction: Oh! You're the farmer who paints. I'm Margot, with the museum. The city one.#$b#I'm here for the old paintings. You found one, didn't you? You'd know. They smell like linseed and regret.$u
margot.dialogue.Mon: Gunther's given me the reading desks. All of them. He says nobody reads on a Monday.$h
margot.dialogue.Tue: You don't make a painting new, you know. You make it able to keep being old.$u
margot.dialogue.Wed: Half my job is waiting for glue to dry. The other half is telling people not to touch things.$7
margot.dialogue.Thu: You've got good bones. Structurally. Not that I was looking.$l
margot.dialogue.Fri: Gus says I can have the spare room as long as I stop explaining varnish to his customers.$u
margot.dialogue.Sat: Have you met Sable? Of course you have. Sable taught me everything worth knowing.#$b#Including how to leave without telling anyone.$s
margot.dialogue.Sun: Don't look! I'm sketching. It's terrible. It's supposed to be terrible, it's a sketch.$a
margot.dialogue.rainy: Rain's good for paintings. Steady and damp and nobody tracking mud in. Well. Fewer people.$7
mail.margot-letter.title: A visitor from the city
mail.margot-letter: Dear @,^^The painting you found has caused quite a stir. I wrote to the Museum of Art in Zuzu City, and they are sending a conservator to see it, and any others the valley turns up.^^Her name is Margot Pell. She arrives next week, and Gus has a room for her. I'm told she talks a great deal.^^   -Gunther
